subject: Ops consolidation: wins, impediments, and QBR actions
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Ops consolidation: wins, impediments, and QBR actions

Good morning — sending a concise weekly exec note focused on the Ops consolidation workstream and QBR inputs. High-level summary first, then asks.

Wins
- Completed model routing smoke tests for the new routing policy (avg p50 latency within target for 75% workloads).
- Prefix cache rollout on Dedicated clusters completed for EU region; metrics show 12% token-cost reduction in last 48h.
- Two pilot customers (Acme AI, Brightly Health) validated failover path during a simulated node outage.

Risks / Impediments
- Capacity gating with CloudVendor: we have a potential 10% shortfall on committed GPUs for Nov- early-Dec windows for Dedicated. (Raised by infra; Vivek is looped.)
- Procurement hold on Acme deal: security team needs a signed DPA amendment before we schedule Dedicated onboarding; Elena from Acme is coordinating but procurement has requested additional documentation.
- QBR pack gaps: we need a short bullet on the expected delta to unit economics from the prefix cache and a headcount ask for 2 SRE contractors to support rollout.

Asks / Next steps
- Laura: include the headcount + cost delta as a discrete slide in the QBR pack (attach numbers to the "cost savings" slide).
- Vivek: confirm CloudVendor fallback options or short-term burst plan by EOD Tue (we need an official mitigation to present at QBR).
- Marissa: please own the updated timeline to share with Acme procurement and confirm what evidence they still need.

Attachments: QBR-deltas.xlsx (contains cost delta table), SLA-exception-request.pdf (draft to present if capacity shortfall persists).

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Head of Platform Ops, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ops consolidation: wins, impediments, and QBR actions

Thanks for the crisp summary — helpful. Two quick notes:

- Please add the explicit headcount ask as a single slide with the budget impact and suggested timing (QBR audience wants clarity: "who/what/when").
- Can we include one anonymized customer quote from the Acme pilot (Elena can approve) showing "reliability improvement" — that helps the narrative.

On the CloudVendor risk: if Vivek confirms a shortfall, I want a concrete fallback in the pack (e.g., canary routing to hosted or a 2-week credit to cover burst). Otherwise we look exposed in the "execution" section.

Appreciate the attachments — I reviewed QBR-deltas.xlsx and left two comments (highlighted cells).

Laura
Laura Bennett
Chief Operating Officer, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ops consolidation: wins, impediments, and QBR actions

Updating the thread with the current state from infra and a forwarded note from CloudOps Sales (below). Short version: there is a confirmed capacity constraint in 2026-11 that will impact throughput if we cannot secure burst or reassign existing pools. I'm pushing three mitigation options and need leadership's preference so we can finalize the slide.

Mitigation options (high-level)
1) Short-term burst agreement with CloudVendor for up to 15% additional capacity — likely a premium rate but fast. (I asked for a firm price; awaiting their confirmation.)
2) Canary more traffic to Hosted (Redwood API) for specific customers during the high-util window — reduces Dedicated availability but preserves SLAs for the tiered customers.
3) Delay non-critical rollouts by 2 weeks and re-prioritize jobs to free GPUs.

My recommendation: sign a capped burst agreement to secure capacity while we throttle lower-priority jobs. If leadership prefers no spend, we'll present option 2 to customers and request their agreement.

Attaching SLA-exception-request.pdf for review. If we go the burst route, we'll present the ask in the QBR as an "execution contingency" and request pre-approval for up to $120k in one-time burst spend.

--Forwarded message--
From: CloudOps Sales <cloudops-sales@cloudvendor.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 11:45:00 -0500
Subject: Capacity update for Nov-Dec window

Hi Vivek,

Quick update: our GPU pool commitments across the west region are tight for Nov 1-21 due to a large retail customer spike. We can do a temporary burst (up to 20%) but the pricing will be at a higher premium tier. If you want to lock in, we need a PO by 10/22.

Regards,
Samir Patel
CloudOps Sales
cloudops-sales@cloudvendor.com

Thanks everyone — quick confirmation of owners and timing so we can close the QBR pack this week.

Decisions / Owners
- Laura: add headcount slide and ensure we have the budget callout (due Tue EOD) — owner: laura_bennett.
- Vivek: confirm CloudVendor burst terms and whether we sign PO by 10/22 — owner: vivek_kulkarni.
- Marissa: follow up with Acme procurement and send a single list of outstanding artifacts to Elena by Mon EOD — owner: marissa_cole.
- Rafael (me): consolidate the QBR slide deck, fold in the cost delta sheet, and prepare a 3-slide "execution contingency" section for the QBR. I will circulate a final pack by Wed 10/20 noon PT.

Elena / Acme: thanks for the pilot participation — Marissa will reach out with the procurement checklist. If Elena can share an approved quote/one-line customer note for the QBR, that'd be very helpful.

I'll schedule a 20-min dry-run on Wed 10/20 at 11:00 AM PT for the exec rundown unless I hear objections.

Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Head of Platform Ops, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
